newsitem.title: COLOMBIA: Colombian stocks end higher, retailer gains.
newsitem.headline: Colombian stocks end higher, retailer gains.

text.p: Colombian stocks ended higher in trading that saw gains led by the country's top bank and largest supermarket chain.

Medellin general price index added 0.42 percent to close at 17,289.86 on trading volume of 2.8 billion pesos. Bogota's rose 0.66 percent, meanwhile, ending at 1,125.65 on above-average volume of 3.8 billion pesos.

Carulla y Compania SA, the leading supermarket chain in Colombia, led movers in Bogota. It rose 2.25 percent to close at 3,400 pesos per share on what brokers described as a fledgling rebound, after recent selling sparked by market concerns about the stock's upside potential.
"The stock took a hard fall over a short period of time and now it's trying to recover," said one Bogota-based broker.

Compania de Cementos Argos was another winner, moving up 1.19 percent in both Bogota and Medellin to end at 8,665 pesos a share on persistent market talks about strong first-quarter earnings. The cement company, which belongs to the Sindicato Antioqueno group, has risen sharply since last week.
"People keep speculating about the cement maker's good first- quarter earnings, but there still aren't any numbers," one trader said.
Winners in Medellin were led by blue-chip Banco Ganadero, which has languished in recent weeks but saw its ordinary shares add 2.23 percent to close at 355 pesos per share.
"Local investors were encouraged by expectations the bank will show good results for the first quarter," a trader said.

Banco de Colombia, which has moved sharply lower on disappointing Q1 earnings and the recent collapse of its partnership talks with Spain's Banco Central Hispano-Americano, managed to edge up 0.26 percent in Bogota and 0.94 in Medellin. It closed in both centers at 375 pesos per share.
